source.title: Understanding Artificial Neural Network's Behavior from Neuron Activation Perspective

record.tranche_reason: The paper discusses neural scaling laws and derives a theoretical loss-versus-dataset-size relationship, but it does not test held-out language-model loss, extrapolation, compute-optimal allocation, or the other listed versions.
record.gate_note: The paper's own result is a theoretical derivation under a stable activation probability assumption, not an empirical measurement of model loss. Results it attributes to other papers, including the cited scaling observations, are excluded.
record.test_reason: Purely theoretical derivation under a stable activation probability hypothesis for a single layer. It reports no measured loss, sweep, fit, extrapolation, allocation or downstream result. Figure 1 only plots the paper's own K(D) formula with chosen constants (N=10^11, c=10^5, b=10^3), not data. It offers an explanation of power-law loss in D, not a test of any version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors claim their activation-process framework explains three things: generalization under over-parameterization, a phase transition in loss against log data size, and power-law loss decay with D. They also give testable predictions on compressibility and capability density. They list open problems: the mechanism of the clustering process, the N dependence via the L_opt term, multi-layer aggregation, and why Transformer shape matters little.
record.recipe_differences: The paper uses a theoretical stochastic neuron-activation framework rather than empirical scaling sweeps and fitted loss curves.

fits_no_version.finding: Under a stable activation probability hypothesis for a single ReLU layer, the paper derives a loss in D of the form L'opt + (L'noise−L'opt)·((b'N')^(1−α)−1)/(c'cD)^(1−α), with 0<α<1. It also derives a phase transition in loss against log D.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A stochastic neuron-activation model yields a theoretically derived power-law decay of loss with dataset size, with a phase transition near cD ≈ bN.

fits_no_version.finding: The paper predicts untested compression effects: larger models are more compressible, and the compression ratio falls with D roughly as a power law.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The fraction of never-activated (free) neurons, and hence compressibility, rises with N and falls with D.

record.problems: The scaling result is theoretical and depends on the paper's activation-probability assumption; there is no empirical validation of the derived loss relationship in the paper. The analysis focuses on a single layer, and the authors identify precise multi-layer aggregation as unresolved.
record.rows_left_out: No other own results directly measure the claim's outcomes. The cited empirical scaling results are from other work and are not recorded as rows.

untested.parts: No empirical held-out loss measured against N, D or C. Power law in D is derived theoretically; the N dependence is left open (L_opt term).
No fits or extrapolation to larger runs.
No compute-optimal allocation measured. The N^0.74∝D relation is cited from Kaplan and only argued to be consistent with the theory.
The shape question is explicitly left open; no architecture comparison.
No other modalities or regimes tested.
No fitting choices or setup variations examined.

record.verdict_notes: Neither original source applies. The paper's Figure 1 is a numerical plot of its own formula, not an experiment. Its cited empirical support (Kaplan Fig. 2, Densing law) is other work and should not become rows.

versions.untested_parts: No held-out pretraining loss is measured; no language-model sweep over parameters, tokens, or compute is performed.
No fitted law or prediction of larger runs is evaluated.
No fixed-compute allocation or parameter/token scaling trend is measured.
The paper says the question of why Transformer shape matters little remains unanswered; it does not compare architectures.
No empirical test of other modalities, repeated data, fine-tuning, or transfer.
No fitting choices or setup variations are tested for their effect on exponents or curve shape.

rows.subject: single layer of neurons in a deep neural network
rows.operation_detail: Theoretical derivation of loss as training dataset size increases, using the paper's activation-process framework.
rows.measure: Derived loss relationship with dataset size
rows.value: Equation (11) gives loss as approximately L′opt + (L′noise − L′opt) times ((b′N′)^(1−α) − 1) / (c′·cD)^(1−α); the paper describes this as a power law in D.
rows.note: This is a theoretical derivation, not an observed held-out loss result; the paper itself notes that deriving the relationship with N requires further analysis.
rows.check: Row is a theoretical derivation (eq. 11), not a measured result. It has no subject model, baseline or value that could show any version's effect. Keep it only as a fits_no_version note, or drop it as a row.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
